s: A trading company runs an Aurora MySQL global database with the primary cluster in eu-west-1 and a secondary cluster in eu-central-1. Regulators require the company to run production from the secondary Region for one week every year to prove the DR capability. Both Regions are healthy during these exercises. The exercise must not lose any committed transactions, and the replication topology must stay intact so that the company can move back afterward. What should a solutions architect do?
o: Perform a global database failover with data loss allowed to eu-central-1, and later add eu-west-1 back as a secondary cluster.
Remove the eu-central-1 cluster from the global database and promote it to a standalone cluster. Re-create the global database after the exercise.
Perform an Aurora global database switchover to eu-central-1, and later perform another switchover back to eu-west-1.
Create a cross-Region read replica in eu-central-1 and promote it at the start of the exercise.

w.y: A switchover (formerly called managed planned failover) is designed for planned operations when both Regions are healthy. It synchronizes the secondary before it changes roles, so the RPO is zero, and it keeps the global topology. The words 'planned', 'no committed transactions lost', and 'topology intact' all point to it.

o.A: Failover with data loss allowed is for unplanned outages and can lose recently committed transactions.
o.B: Detach-and-promote breaks the global database, so the replication setup must be rebuilt.
o.C: Correct: switchover gives zero data loss, keeps the topology, and can be reversed the same way.
o.D: Aurora MySQL binlog-based replicas are a legacy, manual approach. Promoting one breaks replication, and lag can lose data.

d: planned, no data loss, topology intact
